key_insight: World from Motion turns a monocular video into a freely renderable dynamic 3D Gaussian scene, using motion-aware conditioning to recover missing regions and reduce rendering artifacts. In simple terms, it learns a 3D world model from one video that can be viewed from new angles over time.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the challenge of reconstructing high-quality dynamic 3D scenes from only a single camera video, where occlusions, incomplete coverage, and view-dependent artifacts make novel-view rendering difficult.
method: Builds an initial dynamic 3D Gaussian reconstruction from monocular video.
Conditions a video model on dense, pixel-aligned renderings that encode appearance, geometry, and 3D scene motion along both input and target camera paths.
Uses the conditioned model to correct artifacts and hallucinate missing content for more complete, freely renderable dynamic scenes.
Trains on a new dataset of aligned multiview video pairs and dynamic 3DGS representations.
impact: This method makes dynamic scene reconstruction more practical for AR/VR, robotics, digital twins, and content creation by enabling better novel-view synthesis from a single video. For practitioners, it offers a path toward more complete and visually consistent 3D scene representations without requiring expensive capture setups.

paper_title: World from Motion: Generative Dynamic Gaussian Reconstruction from Monocular Video
paper_authors: Liyuan Zhu, Shengyu Huang, Amrita Mazumdar, Tianye Li, Zan Gojcic
